question: Is the 'Southeast Face' stub on Summit Chief Mountain the same climb as the 'South Route'?
answer: Yes, the same climb. The standard route is the scramble Wikipedia and trip reports call the Southeast Face: from the Vista Lakes camp across Vista Ridge to Summit Chief Pass, over sandstone slabs into the southeast basin, up the snowfields to a notch on the south ridge, then loose class 2-3 scrambling to the top. Our South Route row (face field 'Southeast Face / Basin') describes exactly that. No source separates a 'South Route' from the 'Southeast Face'. Reports titled 'Southeast Face-East Ridge' (1986) and 'Southeast Face-Southwest Face' (2013) are finishing variations on the same face, not a separate route.
